title: Telly Renfroe debrief — Tamara Maxwell / EXIM Africa pathway and Valerie Mosley energy lead
summary: Telly Renfroe debriefed Isaac Barnes on conversations with Tamara "Tammy" Maxwell of U.S. EXIM and Valerie Mosley. Tammy asked USG to start each project with the buyer, the seller or U.S. exporter, whether the buyer is governmental or private, and a concise project synopsis; after receiving those facts, she is willing to guide the team through the package requirements. She said she cannot speak for Afreximbank and that its internal rules differ, while characterizing U.S. EXIM as the more stringent screen. Telly also relayed Tammy's report that she is close to completing a process under which selected African banks could underwrite qualifying loans with an EXIM guarantee, potentially reducing approval time for mid-tier transactions up to an indicated $25 million, especially equipment-related transactions. This policy detail remains unverified in writing. Tammy reportedly has expanding access to African development conversations and referenced a national-development project list totaling approximately $209 billion, with approval status and missing requirements shown for each project; the location sounds like Abidjan in the transcript but must be confirmed. Telly further reported that people previously aligned with Tammy are continuing to form a private company focused on packaging transactions for EXIM, other ECAs, and partner banks; because Tammy is a federal official, no commercial engagement should occur without ethics and conflict review. Separately, Valerie Mosley has an energy-related opportunity that may fit EXIM and wants USG to meet relevant people, but the project is not yet sufficiently defined to attach to an initiative or assess for EXIM eligibility. Nonessential personal commentary about Tammy was intentionally excluded from the operational record.
decisions: Treat Tammy Maxwell as a high-value package-readiness guide and relationship node, not as an approval or financing commitment.

Standardize a pre-screen before bringing any opportunity to Tammy: buyer, seller/U.S. exporter, public or private buyer status, project synopsis, country, transaction value, U.S. content, financing request, approvals, and current gaps.
Prioritize one or two qualified U.S.-export-linked equipment or energy transactions at or below the reported $25 million level as test cases once the product pathway is confirmed.
Keep the reported African-bank underwriting process classified as pending policy intelligence until EXIM provides written terms, eligible institutions, and an effective date.
Track Valerie Mosley's energy opportunity as an unqualified lead until the buyer, sponsor, country, value, U.S. export nexus, approvals, and expected USG role are documented.
Do not engage or route compensation to any private packaging venture connected to a serving federal official without written ethics and conflict-of-interest clearance.
risks: The reported delegated-underwriting rule is not yet publicly or directly confirmed in writing, and the $25 million ceiling may refer to financed amount, exposure, or transaction value.
Passing a U.S. EXIM screen does not constitute Afreximbank approval; the institutions have different internal rules and must be approached separately.

EXIM eligibility will depend on facts not yet captured, including U.S. exporter and content, buyer credit, country limitations, transaction structure, tenor, environmental or economic-impact review, and available lender participation.
The reported $209 billion development-project list, its country or institution, and the transcript's apparent reference to Abidjan require confirmation before use.
The transcript contains one unclear reference to a party or prior discussion rendered as "advanced" or similar; it should not be treated as a named source until Telly clarifies it.
Any overlap between Tammy's federal duties and a private packaging enterprise presents ethics, procurement-integrity, and conflict-of-interest risk that requires counsel review.

next_actions.action: Create a reusable EXIM/Afreximbank opportunity intake sheet covering buyer, seller/U.S. exporter, public-private status, project synopsis, country, value, U.S. content, financing request, development stage, approvals, lender/ECA history, and missing documents.
Identify one to three existing Africa opportunities that have a clear U.S. export nexus and could be scoped at or below $25 million for initial package-readiness review.

Send Tammy concise pre-screen summaries for the strongest candidate projects and request the current written checklist, product fit, process sequence, named relationship owner, and status of the reported African-bank underwriting pathway.

Circle back with Valerie Mosley and capture the energy project's name, country, buyer or sponsor, public-private status, value, U.S. exporter/content, approvals, financing need, proposed introductions, and the role she expects USG to perform.

Confirm whether the transcript's location was Abidjan, identify the owner/source of the approximately $209 billion development-project list, and request the list or a shareable subset showing approvals and gaps.
Clarify the transcript's reference rendered as "advanced" or similar and identify the person, company, or prior conversation being cited in connection with Valerie's energy lead.
Complete legal and ethics review before any referral, compensation, teaming, or transaction-packaging engagement involving a private venture connected to a serving EXIM official.
